title: How to handle lone surrogates in filenames in form submission

labels.name: i18n-tracker
labels.description: Group bringing to attention of Internationalization, or tracked by i18n but not needing response.

labels.name: interop
labels.description: Implementations are not interoperable with each other

body:
The `name` property of `File` objects is a `DOMString`, rather than a scalar value string. And although [there is no way to programatically create](https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/issues/31645) a `File` object with lone surrogates in its filename, Windows systems do allow lone surrogates in filenames, so you could end up with such an object resulting from an `<input type="file">`.

This is a problem because, unlike string values, the filenames of `File` values in a form's entry list are not converted [when the entry is created](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/form-control-infrastructure.html#create-an-entry), or at any point after that. With the `multipart/form-data` enctype, the filenames are passed to the [encode](https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#encode) algorithm, which expects a scalar value string ([or anything else that converts to an I/O queue of scalar values](https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#to-i-o-queue-convert)). Similarly, for the other enctypes, the filename is extracted in ["convert to a list of name-value pairs"](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/form-control-infrastructure.html#convert-to-a-list-of-name-value-pairs), but not converted to a scalar value string, and that is also ultimately passed to "encode", whether in the urlencoded serializer, or in the form submission algorithm.

Here's what the different browser engines do:
- Firefox always converts to a scalar value string. When the form charset is UTF-8, lone surrogates are correctly encoded as the replacement character, and for other encodings, they're encoded as `�`, the charref corresponding to the replacement character.
- Chromium's behavior differs depending on the enctype:
  - For the `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` and `text/plain` enctypes, filenames are always converted to a scalar value string, and Chromium behaves the same as Firefox.
  - With `multipart/form-data`, when the form charset is UTF-8, lone surrogates are correctly encoded as the replacement character, but for other encodings, they're encoded as a charref for the surrogate code point (`�`, for example).
- WebKit leaves lone surrogates as is. When the form charset is UTF-8, lone surrogates are encoded as invalid UTF-8 (see [the WTF-8 encoding](https://simonsapin.github.io/wtf-8/)), and for other encodings, they're encoded as a charref for the surrogate code point.

Note that since the input to the "encode" algorithm must be a scalar value string, any character references emitted as a replacement for unencodable characters must correspond to scalar values, so if we were to enshrine Chromium's or WebKit's behavior into the spec, it would need changes to the encoding standard. Hopefully that is not necessary and we can settle on always converting to a scalar value string.

cc @mfreed7 @cdumez
